properties.natural_language: Before a community member proposes a new origin via EDGE-PROPOSAL-SUBMIT, the origin must have a publicly accessible URL and a clearly identifiable resource catalog
Before evaluation begins via EDGE-START-EVAL, the proposed origin must have a complete submission with sufficient documentation for editors to assess all three mandatory criteria
After unique identification check succeeds via EDGE-ID-OK, the origin must have at least one verified method (git hash, version number, or date) for uniquely identifying resource revisions
After approval via EDGE-APPROVE, the origin must be listed in EIP-1 with proper formatting specifications and all three requirements verified
The evaluation must follow strict sequential ordering: unique identification check -> availability check -> free access check, with no step skipped or reordered
Any failure at any evaluation step (identification, availability, or free access) must result in transition to REJECTED state with no possibility of approval
EIP editors must consistently evaluate all origins against the same mandatory criteria without applying different standards
Before validation begins via EDGE-START-VALIDATION, the origin candidate must be in a well-defined state with accessible resources for testing
After all validation passes via EDGE-COST-OK, the origin must satisfy all three requirements: revision identification, 10+ year availability, and zero cost access
At least one of git hash, version number, or publication date must be available for revision identification to be considered valid
The availability longevity requirement must enforce a minimum threshold (10 years as strong benchmark) with editor discretion for shorter histories
Free access means no monetary cost for accessing resources; account registration without payment may be acceptable
Before violation detection via EDGE-DETECT, the origin must be in an active approved state listed in EIP-1
After removal via EDGE-REMOVED, the origin must no longer appear in the approved origins list and existing EIP references must be flagged
The removal-to-reapproval lifecycle must follow the complete path: violation detected -> removed -> fixed -> reapply -> re-approved, with no shortcuts
External origin providers must not be able to bypass the re-evaluation process after a violation has been detected
Before blob retrieval via EDGE-BLOCK-NEEDS-DA, the block must have passed initial validation and contain valid KZG commitments
Before KZG batch verification via EDGE-BLOBS-RETRIEVED, all blobs and their corresponding KZG proofs must be retrieved from the P2P blob sidecar network
After successful KZG verification via EDGE-KZG-VALID, all blobs must be cryptographically proven to match their commitments in the block header
A block must never transition to DATA-AVAILABLE state if any blob fails KZG proof verification or if any required blob is missing
Extraneous or invalid blobs from the network must not cause rejection of otherwise-valid blocks
Before on_block processing via EDGE-START-ON-BLOCK, the block's parent must exist in the fork choice store
After store update via EDGE-STORE-UPDATED, the block and its resulting state must be persisted in the store with timeliness recorded and checkpoints updated
The on_block handler must enforce strict sequential verification: parent exists -> timing valid -> finalization lineage -> data available -> state transition -> store update
Any assertion failure at any verification step must cause block rejection with no partial state updates to the store
Once a block passes data availability check and is added to the store, it retains its valid status even if blobs are later pruned
Before building PayloadAttributes via EDGE-PREPARE-ATTRS, the proposer must have valid timestamp, prev_randao, fee recipient, withdrawals, and parent beacon block root
Before sending forkchoiceUpdated to the execution engine via EDGE-SEND-TO-EE, the PayloadAttributes must include the parent_beacon_block_root field required by EIP-4788
After the execution engine receives the forkchoiceUpdated call via EDGE-EE-BUILDING, it must begin constructing a valid execution payload using all provided attributes
Before difficulty calculation via EDGE-BLOCK-PRODUCTION, the block producer must provide valid parent block data and current block number from a trusted source
After fake block number computation via EDGE-FAKE-NUM-READY, the adjusted block number must equal actual_block_number - 10,700,000, and must be non-negative
After final difficulty computation via EDGE-DIFF-DONE, the difficulty value must be the sum of homestead adjustment and bomb component, and must be at least the minimum difficulty
The difficulty bomb component must be computed as 2^((fake_block_number // 100000) - 2), and due to the 10,700,000 offset, its effect is negligible during Arrow Glacier's active period
The difficulty calculation pipeline must follow strict order: fake block number -> bomb component -> final difficulty, with no step bypassed
Before fork activation check via EDGE-NEW-BLOCK-RECEIVED, the network peer must provide a valid block header with an authentic block number
After fork activation via EDGE-FORK-ACTIVE, the system must use the Arrow Glacier difficulty calculation with the 10,700,000 offset for all subsequent blocks
Fork activation must be deterministic: blocks with number < 13,773,000 always use pre-Arrow Glacier rules, blocks >= 13,773,000 always use Arrow Glacier rules
Before block header validation via EDGE-RECEIVE-HEADER, the peer must provide a block header with claimed difficulty and parent hash referencing a known block
After difficulty comparison via EDGE-MATCH, the claimed difficulty must exactly equal the computed expected difficulty under Arrow Glacier rules
After block rejection via EDGE-REJECTED, the invalid block must not be added to the chain or propagated to other peers
Difficulty validation must be deterministic: given the same parent block and block number, the expected difficulty must always be the same value
A difficulty mismatch must always lead to block rejection; there is no tolerance for approximate matches
Before emptiness check via EDGE-CHECK-EMPTY, the account must have been touched by a qualifying operation during transaction execution
After deletion via EDGE-DELETED, the account must be completely removed from the state trie with no residual data
An account is empty if and only if nonce=0, balance=0, and code is empty; storage state is irrelevant for this determination
Only empty accounts can be deleted; accounts with any non-zero nonce, balance, or code must always be preserved
Before any touch trigger executes, a transaction must be actively executing in the EVM
After any touch operation (zero-value CALL, CREATE, SELFDESTRUCT, tx target, or miner fee), the target address must be marked as touched for end-of-transaction emptiness evaluation
All five touch triggers (zero-value CALL, CREATE, SELFDESTRUCT, transaction target, miner fee recipient) must result in the same ADDRESS-TOUCHED state
Before target existence check via EDGE-CHECK-EXISTS, a zero-value CALL or SELFDESTRUCT must be in progress
Post-EIP-158, zero-value operations to nonexistent targets must never charge the 25,000 gas account creation cost
Pre-EIP-158, zero-value operations to nonexistent targets must always charge 25,000 gas for account creation
Before cheap touch exploitation via EDGE-CHEAP-ACCESS, legacy empty accounts from the pre-EIP-158 era must exist in the state trie
The vulnerability window for cheap state churn must be bounded: once all empty accounts are cleared, the attack surface is eliminated
Contracts must not rely on the distinction between empty and nonexistent accounts for security-critical logic, as EIP-158 eliminates this distinction
Before checking committee assignment via EDGE-EPOCH-CHECK, the validator must be at an epoch boundary with access to the current beacon state
Before retrieving inclusion list from execution engine via EDGE-GET-IL, the validator must have either received a block or timed out (~67% minus 1000ms of slot)
After broadcast via EDGE-BROADCAST, the signed inclusion list must have been sent to the P2P network before the submission deadline (~67% into slot)
The inclusion list must be signed using BLS with DOMAIN_INCLUSION_LIST_COMMITTEE and must include the correct slot, validator_index, and committee_root
An empty inclusion list is valid when the execution engine returns no transactions requiring forced inclusion
Before computing attester head via EDGE-ATTEST-DUE, the validator must have an attestation duty for the current slot
The attester head must return the parent block if the fork choice head is inclusion-list-unsatisfied, ensuring attestations incentivize IL compliance
Before collecting inclusion lists via EDGE-PROPOSER-STARTS, the proposer must have a block proposer duty for the current slot
After block proposal via EDGE-PROPOSED, the execution payload must include all mandated inclusion list transactions
Inclusion lists must only be collected up to PROPOSER_INCLUSION_LIST_CUTOFF_BPS (~92% of previous slot), not after
Before block lookup via EDGE-CLIENT-REQUEST, the RPC client must provide a valid 32-byte block hash and a full transaction flag
After response construction for post-1559 blocks via EDGE-RESPONSE-READY-WITH-BASEFEE, the response must include baseFee formatted as a hexadecimal Quantity string
After response construction for pre-1559 blocks via EDGE-RESPONSE-READY-NO-BASEFEE, the response must NOT include the baseFee field
Fork determination must be deterministic: blocks below the EIP-1559 fork block always omit baseFee, blocks at or above always include it
The baseFee value in the response must exactly match the authentic value stored in the block header without modification
Before field validation via EDGE-START-VALIDATION, the block fork context must be determined from the block number
baseFee format must use standard Ethereum Quantity encoding: 0x prefix, hexadecimal, no leading zeros except for zero value
Before block storage search via EDGE-INITIATE-SEARCH, the lookup must have been initiated with a valid block hash
After null response generation via EDGE-SEND-NULL, the client must receive a valid JSON-RPC response with null result field
When a block hash is not found in storage, the response must always be null, never an error or empty object
Before JUMP execution via EDGE-POP-DEST, the stack must have at least 1 element for the destination address
After successful JUMP via EDGE-JUMP-DONE, the program counter must be set to exactly the validated jump destination
Gas must always be charged (GAS_MID=8) before destination validation; an invalid destination still consumes gas
A jump to an address not in valid_jump_destinations must always raise InvalidJumpDestError and halt execution
Before JUMPI execution via EDGE-POP-JUMPI, the stack must have at least 2 elements: destination and condition
When condition is zero (false), JUMPI must increment PC by 1 without validating or jumping to the destination
When condition is non-zero (true), JUMPI must validate the destination against valid_jump_destinations before jumping
GAS_HIGH (10 gas) must always be charged for JUMPI regardless of the condition value or destination validity
Before STOP execution via EDGE-STOP-DETECTED, the EVM must be in an executing state
After STOP execution via EDGE-STOPPED, evm.running must be False and the program counter must have been incremented
STOP must set running=False before incrementing PC, ensuring the halt flag is set even though PC increment is performed
Before PC or GAS opcode execution, the EVM must be in a running state with sufficient gas (at least GAS_BASE=2)
The GAS opcode must push the gas_left value AFTER charging GAS_BASE, not before, reflecting remaining gas at that execution point
Both PC and GAS opcodes share the same GAS_BASE cost (2 gas) and both must increment the program counter after execution
Before any jump validation, the contract bytecode must have been scanned and valid_jump_destinations set must be populated
Before contract code scanning, the contract deployer must have provided bytecode that is loaded into the EVM
JUMPDEST scanning must correctly skip over PUSH data bytes to avoid treating 0x5b data bytes as valid jump destinations
JUMPDEST (0x5b) execution charges only GAS_JUMPDEST (1 gas) and is a no-op that marks valid landing points
Any jump to an address not marked by JUMPDEST in the whitelist must result in an InvalidJumpError state
Before Type 1 transaction processing via EDGE-RECEIVE-TX, the transaction submitter must provide a properly signed transaction with 0x01 prefix
After access list pre-warming via EDGE-WARMED, all addresses and storage keys from the access list must be in the warm access sets
After access list gas charging via EDGE-GAS-CHARGED, the sender must have been charged 2400 per address + 1900 per storage key in the access list
Access list format validation must reject lists where any address is not exactly 20 bytes or any storage key is not exactly 32 bytes
Signature verification must be performed over keccak256(0x01 || rlp([chainId, nonce, gasPrice, gasLimit, to, value, data, accessList])) with the access list included in the signed data
Transaction processing must follow strict order: decode -> validate format -> verify signature -> charge gas -> pre-warm -> execute
Before gas calculation via EDGE-START-CALC, the transaction validation stage must provide the transaction type and access list
Duplicate entries in the access list must be charged gas (2400 per address, 1900 per key) even though they provide no additional warm access benefit
Pre-warmed storage access via SLOAD must cost 100 gas, while cold SLOAD costs 2100 gas, making the access list economically beneficial for known accesses
Pre-warmed address access via EXT* opcodes must cost 100 gas, while cold access costs 2600 gas
Total intrinsic gas must equal base intrinsic (21000 + calldata) + access list gas (n*2400 + m*1900)
Before transaction type check via EDGE-RECEIVE-BYTES, raw transaction bytes must be received from a network peer
Chain ID validation must reject transactions targeting different networks, preventing cross-chain replay attacks
Each access list entry must have exactly one 20-byte address and zero or more 32-byte storage keys
Before access set initialization via EDGE-INIT-SETS, the transaction execution must be starting with a valid access list
Default warming must always include sender, recipient, and all precompile addresses before processing the access list
Duplicate addresses or keys in the access list must be silently accepted (added to set, which deduplicates) but gas is still charged for each
After all entries are processed, every address and (address, key) tuple from the access list must be present in the respective warm sets
Before gossip message validation, the message must be received from a peer on a subscribed topic with proper encoding
After message rejection via any invalid edge, the peer may be penalized according to peer scoring rules
KZG commitment count in beacon blocks must not exceed MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK_ELECTRA; exceeding this limit must cause rejection
Aggregate attestation committee_bits must have exactly 1 bit set and aggregate data index must equal 0 in Electra format
Single attestation data index must be 0 and the attester must be a verified member of the committee for the given slot
Blob sidecar index and commitments must be validated against MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK_ELECTRA limits
Before processing any req/resp request, a valid request must be received from a peer on one of the defined protocol streams
Blob sidecar requests must be limited to MAX_REQUEST_BLOB_SIDECARS_ELECTRA; exceeding this limit must return an error response
Block responses must use fork-appropriate SignedBeaconBlock types, including electra.SignedBeaconBlock for slots at or after the Electra fork
Before publishing a SingleAttestation to a subnet, the validator must have created a valid attestation object
Attestation validation must verify both committee membership and data.index==0 constraint before propagating to other peers
Before version negotiation via EDGE-PEER-CONNECTS, a valid TCP connection must be established with the peer node
After handshake completion, both peers must agree on the same protocol version (v4 uncompressed or v5 compressed)
Version negotiation must use minimum of local and remote versions: if either peer only supports v4, the session must use v4 (uncompressed)
Hello messages must be exchanged before any compressed messages are sent; version negotiation must complete before data transfer
Before compression check via EDGE-SUBPROTOCOL-MSG, a subprotocol must emit a valid message for transmission
Snappy compression must use raw block format without framing, as DEVp2p is already message-oriented
All messages must be encrypted via RLPx regardless of whether compression is applied; encryption always follows compression
When compression is disabled (v4), messages must bypass Snappy and go directly to encryption
Before decompression processing via EDGE-RECEIVE, encrypted bytes must be received from the network TCP socket
Decompressed message size must not exceed 16MB; messages exceeding this limit must be rejected before decompression
Decryption must always occur before decompression check; the receive pipeline is: decrypt -> check compression -> (decompress if v5) -> dispatch
Both compressed and uncompressed paths must ultimately dispatch to the same subprotocol handler
Before security checks via EDGE-ATTACKER-SENDS, the system must be prepared to receive potentially malicious compressed payloads from any peer
Varint overflow (> 2^32-1) must always be detected and result in connection termination before any decompression attempt
Decompression bombs must be detected by checking declared size against 16MB limit BEFORE performing actual decompression
Security validation must follow strict order: varint check -> size limit check -> decompression, with early termination on any failure
The Snappy library must be free of buffer overflow vulnerabilities; malformed compressed data must not lead to remote code execution
